summary: A 1928 L-5 log-and-frame ground house on the Lolo NF near the Idaho line; unstaffed since before 1965 and partly restored in 2019.

facts.design: L-5 log and frame ground house with mortise-and-tenon log joints
facts.status_note: Standing but leaning and rotting at the base when last reported (2011); first restoration phase done in 2019; roof work still awaiting funding

staffing.as_of: per NHLR and firelookout.com, both undated

access.note: No rental or permit listed in the sources read; unclear whether the cabin interior is open to visitors

visit.trail_note: 2011 visit report: trail in good condition with new water bars; directions signed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 6,772 ft (2,064 m). The 2019 Missoula Current article and firelookout.com both give 7,215 ft (about 2,199 m). The record keeps the register figure as the most formal source; these sources do not settle which figure is right.
The register places the lookout in Missoula County, Montana. firelookout.com places it in Idaho County, Idaho. The site sits on the state line; the record keeps Missoula County.

sources.title: Skookum Butte: Volunteers save historic lookout for the ages

notes_for_editor: The build year, L-5 design and 1996 register date agree across sources. Elevation and county disagree between the register and the two later sources; the record keeps the register values. Restoration: the 2019 article describes a first phase only, and roof work was still pending. Access is unknown: no rental or permit was found, and the story tells visitors to check with the Lolo National Forest. The firelookout.com Idaho-region URL returned 404; the Montana page was used instead. Staffing dates differ slightly (before 1965 in the register; early 1960s on firelookout.com) and are reported that way.
